verdict.rationale: Google's security-key docs say that to sign in with just the security key and skip the password, you must create a passkey, which implies the key can hold passkey credentials. The rest of the evidence only cites FIDO CTAP1 (U2F) compatibility for third-party sites and never confirms resident/discoverable credential storage or username-less sign-in. missing for 10: explicit FIDO2/CTAP2 resident-key (discoverable credential) support, documentation of username-less sign-in, storage capacity/management details, evidence for third-party WebAuthn services beyond Google, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the key stores discoverable FIDO2 credentials (resident keys / device-bound passkeys) so users can sign in to WebAuthn services without typing a username

citations.quote: If you want to sign in with just your security key and skip your password when possible, you must create a passkey.
